point: Separating policy and planning (DWR), resource regulation and allocation, and economic regulation of utilities (a separate Water Regulatory Commission) follows international practice and is preferable
The Senate bills should be consolidated into a substitute bill, drawing on HB 6789, which the House approved on third and final reading and transmitted to the Senate
keywords: third reading|third and final|transmitted|approved by the house;senate|substitute|consolidat

point: Short titles differ: HB 6789 uses National Water Resources Management Act; some Senate bills use Department of Water Resources Act
keywords: national water resources management act|short title

point: HB 6789 lets the DWR deputize agents from the public or private sector; deputizing only government officials avoids conflicts of interest
A Water Resources Allocation Board (HB 6789) fits better than an Adjudication Board, since regulating water rights is first about allocating permits
HB 6789's Water Trust Fund would need new fund managers and untested accountability; socialized credit through government financing institutions is preferable
Declaring water a public good is incorrect; it is a common-pool resource (rival, non-excludable)
Institutional reform alone will not fix perpetual water permits and the lack of volumetric accounting unless PD 1067 (Water Code) is amended
PD 1067 predates climate change: no provisions on drought allocation, climate variability or water security planning
Permit revocation powers are limited while PD 1067 governs; best practice is time-bound permits and basin-level allocation limits
